The Chamber refers to the Prosecution's motion to exclude the evidence of Witness Snezana Kovac filed on the 30th of January, 2013, and the accused's response to that motion filed on the 4th of February, 2013, which includes the accused's motion for admission of Snezana Kovac's statement pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Having also considered the Prosecution response to the Defence motion for admission of the statement of Snezana Kovac pursuant to Rule 92 bis filed on 5th of February, 2013, the Chamber now issues its decision on both motions. At the outset, the Chamber notes that the accused in his response states that the Trial Chamber's time might be better spent hearing live witnesses whose testimony is more significant than that of Ms. Kovac. As a compromise, he then offers that relevant portions of Ms. Kovac's evidence, in this case, only five paragraphs of her statement, be admitted into evidence pursuant to Rule 92 bis. The accused is reminded that it is incumbent on him to choose his witnesses carefully and not to prepare statements which contain large portions of irrelevant material. It is also inappropriate for the accused to seek to first tender the evidence of a witness pursuant to Rule 92 ter, and when it becomes apparent that large portions of that evidence might be struck out for lack of relevance to then take a selection of potentially relevant paragraphs from that proposed witness statement and seek to tender that pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Contrary to the accused's submission, this does not constitute good cause for the Chamber to allow the admission of such a statement after the 27th of August, 2012, dead-line for the submission of Rule 92 bis motions. In any event, having reviewed Ms. Kovac's original statement and the five paragraphs in Ms. Kovac's revised statement, the Chamber finds that both the original statement and the revised statement are of limited relevance and of such low probative value that Ms. Kovac's evidence should be excluded in its entirety. For the foregoing reasons, the Chamber grants the Prosecution motion to exclude the evidence of Witness Snezana Kovac and denies the accused's motion for admission of statement of Snezana Kovac pursuant to Rule 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could make your -- make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Dr. Trifkovic.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.text: Kindly pause between questions and answers, and you're free to remind me as well, because we both speak Serbian. The interpreters need some time for their work to be done, especially if they go into French. Dr. Trifkovic, did you provide a statement to my Defence team?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I have. As far as I remember it was in early July last year, 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Do you see your statement --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC

utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness should be cautioned to pause before answering, otherwise there will be an overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're not using any headphones so please bear in mind that Mr. Karadzic's words are to be interpreted into English, so you're not to overlap with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So your answer was not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does, with one small addendum that the precise timing of the meeting on 12th of July of 1995 was given as between 700 [sic] and 1840, and in my original statement I said it was around 5.00 and lasted for about an hour and a half. utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please assist us, what paragraph is that and do you have a hard copy of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have a print-out which I believe to be identical to page 1 which I see on the screen and it refers to page 4, paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Save for that correction, if I were to ask the same questions today, would your answers be basically the same as they are contained in the statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: They would be indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this statement under Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, but before that, what -- what did you mean by your original statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The verbal statement I gave to a member of the team in Belgrade in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Karadzic, you are not tendering any associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Vanderpuye, do you have any objection to the admission of his Rule 92 ter statement?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read out a summary of Dr. Trifkovic's statement in English. [In English] Dr. Srdja Trifkovic is currently foreign affairs editor of the monthly magazine "Chronicles" published in the Rockford Institute in Illinois, USA. He is a former Chief of Staff to Crown Prince Alexander Karadjordjevic based in London, England. In that capacity, Dr. Trifkovic met Radovan Karadzic on two occasions in 1993. Beginning in September 1993, Dr. Trifkovic started maintaining occasional communication with the Republika Srpska leadership in his capacity of the -- of Balkan affairs analyst and journalist. He was granted such access in view of his balanced and professional approach to the complex issue of the Bosnian war. In that capacity, he met Dr. Karadzic on a few occasions in 1993-1994, and again in January, March and July 1995. During the day of 13th of July, 1995, Dr. Trifkovic was in Pale and had a meeting with Professor Koljevic. Professor Koljevic was planning to go to Srebrenica the following day, as he put it, to provide reassurance to the civilians of Srebrenica that they would be treated properly. Dr. Trifkovic met with Dr. Karadzic on 13th of July, 1995, from what was corrected today, from 1700 to 18 hours, 40 minutes. He was with Tomislav Premovic and Slavica Ristic. While in his office, Dr. Karadzic was trying to make a telephone connection with the VRS headquarter in Han Pijesak but was told the line was down. Dr. Trifkovic is sure that Dr. Karadzic did not speak to General Mladic during this meeting but with someone from the VRS command. When Dr. Karadzic picked up the phone, Dr. Trifkovic picked up the receiver that was connected to the same line in order to ask General Mladic for a statement that he could quote in his media appearances, but on the other side of the line was not General Mladic but an officer from the VRS headquarters who informed Karadzic about situation in Srebrenica. Dr. Karadzic then turned on the speakerphone so that other guests could hear what was discussed. During this conversation, Dr. Karadzic was insistent that civilians not be mistreated and the conduct of the Serbs in Srebrenica be above reproach so that this could not be used against the Serbs in media. Dr. Trifkovic met with Dr. Karadzic again in the company of Jovan Zametica on 14th of July, 1994, from 2305 hours until 35 minutes after midnight. There was no discussion about prisoners from Srebrenica during his meetings with Dr. Karadzic. On the base of his impressions, based on his previous meetings with Dr. Karadzic, Dr. Trifkovic would find it hard to believe that Dr. Karadzic would condone executing prisoners, not only for pragmatic reasons but also a matter of principle. And that would be summary. I don't have additional questions. Thank you.

utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Trifkovic, as you have now noted, your evidence in chief in this case has been admitted in writing in lieu of your oral testimony. Now you'll be cross-examined by the representative of the Office of the Prosecutor --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I believe we're still in morning so good morning to you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Dr. Trifkovic. The first thing I want to clarify is the record. At page 48 of today's transcript, line 2, you indicated, and I'm sure you misspoke, that the date of your meeting with Dr. Karadzic was on 12 July --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it was actually the 13th, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, you've testified on at least a couple of occasions before this Tribunal; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. And actually on one of those occasions I was crossed by you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that would have been in the Popovic case?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Beara, yes, September '08.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Kindly pause between questions and answers. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also testified in the Stakic case.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at that time I was an expert witness, whereas in September '08 I was actually material witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And your Stakic testimony was during March of 2003; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At the very beginning of the questioning by Dr. Karadzic just today, you indicated that you have a statement with you, a printed copy of your --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- of the statement that is now in evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Or a version of that statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I -- I believe it's actually identical to the one that we have on the screen in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you indicated that there was a clarification made to a previous statement that you made, an oral one that you gave in Belgrade in July of 2012; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Only on this one particular detail concerning the time of the meeting, paragraph 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And what was the nature of the clarification? You said that there was more detail about the time --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- what was the time that you originally gave --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please pause between the questions and the answers, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Are you not hearing the interpreters' note?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's very strange. They have difficulty following both of you. Please pause between the questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. We were -- shall we begin again? Mr. Vanderpuye, could you take a look at the transcript, line 13. So could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What was the particular detail that was clarified from your original statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Only that what I remember saying in my original statement, that the meeting was around 5.00 and went on for approximately an hour and a half. In the written statement it was specified to have been between 1700 and 1840 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that time agrees with your present recollection; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I would not have known with this degree of precision, but it certainly does agree with my overall recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not the oral statement that you gave in July 2012 was reduced to a written statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the written statement that we have here is more or less verbatim transcript of the oral statement that I gave to a member of Dr. Karadzic's team in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When was the written statement that you have there in front of you prepared? When was that printed out and given to you?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Shortly after my oral statement was given. I don't remember exactly, but it could have been a couple of weeks thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. So just so I'm clear, you were aware of no contemporaneous written reduction of your oral statement to the Defence in Belgrade in July of 2012 other than what you have before you and what was introduced into evidence in this case?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any discrepancies or variances between my oral statement and the written version we have here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thanks. When did you first meet with the Defence in connection with the possibility of your testifying in this case?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, actually, the meet -- my giving the oral testimony in July of last year was the first meeting. Prior to that, there had been some e-mails exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: About how far prior to that first meeting did you begin exchanging e-mails with the Defence concerning the possibility of your testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It was sometime in spring. I can't remember exactly whether it was late April, early May, but sometime in the spring of 2012.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in terms of your contacts with the Defence regarding the possibility of your testimony in this case, was the subject matter of your testimony broached?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. The initial approach concerned the possibility of my testifying about the meetings in the summer of 1995. That was, in fact, the purpose of the initial approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Was that discussed in the e-mails that you exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Approximately -- let me pause for a moment. Approximately how many e-mails were exchanged in that period of time between April and July -- or, rather -- yes, April and July?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Very few. I was asked if I would be prepared to testify. I replied affirmatively, and then I was informed that a member of the team would be coming to Belgrade and that he would give me a call. So really, I don't think there were more than three or four.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You met with the Defence in July 2012 in Belgrade, as you've said. Do you remember what date that meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I -- I really don't. In fact, it could have easily been late June, because I know I received the document in July, but it was summer. I remember positively that it was already quite hot.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How many members of the Defence team did you meet with --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- during that summer?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And who was that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It was Marko Sladojevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: How long did you meet with Marko Sladojevic in July or possibly June 2012?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: For about an hour and a half. It was longer than an hour, it was less than two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you discuss with Mr. Sladojevic the subject matter of your testimony or, rather, the subject matter of your statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, it was on that occasion that I gave my verbal statement which he taped and transcribed and sent back to me in the written form.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, did you say that he taped that statement?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I remember, he actually was taking -- taping my voice at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You didn't receive a copy of that tape, right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was he taking notes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: He was also taking notes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you didn't receive a copy of those notes, did you?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And did he take notes throughout the period of time that he was speaking to you regarding the events that you were -- your evidence was to cover?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, he was taking them on and off, but notebook was in evidence all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You met with him for about an hour -- between an hour and two hours --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember where the meeting took place?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting took place at a law office in Belgrade. It's in a suburban area of Belgrade. The name of the law office I don't remember, but it was in a private villa converted for use as -- as an office.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you meet with Mr. Sladojevic or any other member of the Defence team at any point subsequent to this meeting that may have -- that occurred either in June or July of 2012, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not until my arrival here at The Hague when I had a brief meeting with Mr. Robinson on the evening of my arrival on Monday, the day before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The day before yesterday. Did you meet with anybody besides Mr. Robinson prior to testifying here today?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I also had a coffee with Mr. Sladojevic and one of the interns at the hotel yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you discuss the subject matter of your testimony with either Mr. Robinson or Mr. Sladojevic between the time that you arrived on Monday and your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: With Mr. Sladojevic the discussion was more about the questions I am likely to be asked rather than my own testimony, and with Mr. Robinson it was simply the confirmation that the testimony in its written form basically stands and that there are no amendments or changes that I wish to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You didn't discuss the tape recording of your previous statement or the notes that Mr. Sladojevic took during the course of your meeting in Belgrade with either Mr. Robinson or Mr. Sladojevic following your arrival; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you didn't receive it; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have an opportunity to meet with Dr. Karadzic before you testified here today since your arrival?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I met Dr. Karadzic yesterday here in the court building between 1505 and 1600.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you discuss with him the subject matter of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You did. And what exactly did you discuss with him concerning your testimony?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, simply recouping the substance of the testimony and confirming that this is more or less what I have to say, and then we actually moved on to different topics that are not really even related to the court case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In terms of, you say, recouping the substance of your testimony, what do you mean by that exactly?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: In particular, the meeting on the 13th of July and that my recollection of the course -- of the most significant detail of that meeting is -- is solid, which it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: What is the most significant detail of that meeting, Mr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That the call that was put through from Dr. Karadzic's office to the BSA headquarters was not, in fact, connected to General Mladic but to some other officer at the HQ.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you discussed that with Dr. Karadzic yesterday, the day before?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, when we simply -- we didn't really discuss it. We just confirmed that the statement stands and that there are no addenda or changes required.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You discussed that same topic with Mr. Sladojevic when you met him back in July or June of last year?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I say, when I met with Mr. Sladojevic last summer, I actually made the statement, so I didn't discuss it, so to say. I was really putting the statement together rather than discussing its details, and he was more in the role of taking notes and then preparing the written summary which I received by e-mail a couple of weeks later.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And I just want to cover one last issue and that is in your exchange of e-mails with the Defence, before the meeting that occurred in Belgrade, did you discuss this very important detail concerning the meeting of the 13th of July, 1995, in Dr. Karadzic's office in Pale?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: We didn't discuss the details of the meeting itself, but it was indicated to me that the focus of my requested testimony would be on -- on that meeting. In other words, while in the e-mails the details of the meeting were not covered, I was made aware that that particular meeting would be the subject of my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well. So prior to testifying here today, it's fair to say that you've had a number of contacts with the Defence team --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I had --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- concerning your testimony or evidence regarding that 13 July meeting?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had one encounter with Mr. Sladojevic in Belgrade, one with Mr. Robinson at the hotel on Monday evening. I met with Dr. Karadzic yesterday afternoon, and I had a brief meeting with Mr. Sladojevic at the hotel again late afternoon yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Dr. Karadzic began by indicating that you were an editor for "Chronicles," which is a magazine; yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It's a monthly magazine, yes, and I'm foreign affairs editor.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Foreign affairs editor for "Chronicles." How long have you held that position, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Since 1998 with the one-year disruption between the fall of 2008 and the end of 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So all in all, about 14 years? Is that about right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I just want to jump back for a period of time. Back in 1993, you essentially took on a role as a media spokesperson, as it were, for the Republika Srpska leadership; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not fair to say that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: At no time was there any institutionalised or hierarchical connection, and in all of my media appearances I presented myself as a Balkan affairs analyst with close links to the Bosnian Serb leadership but not as their spokesman or representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It is a fact, though, that you have been referred to in the media as such a spokesperson; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been referred to in the media in all kinds of ways, and of course, such references do not necessarily reflect the realities of the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So that's a yes.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been referred in that way to -- and as I said, I've also been referred to in various other ways, complimentary or otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We'll get to those.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But you have been referred to in the media as a spokesperson for the Republika Srpska leadership?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been erroneously referred to in the media in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And it is also a fact that the RS leadership and Dr. Karadzic in particular never disavowed publicly any such association; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: That I wouldn't know, but my visits to Dr. Karadzic during the two-year period on six or seven occasions were not frequent enough for me to know either whether they're aware of such media references or whether they reacted to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you tell them about it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Not specifically. Frankly, I don't think that what some third party may or may not have said about me matters. I think it's far more important in my media appearances, interviews, and writings how I was presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: And invariably in those I was presented not as a spokesman but actually as an analyst with links or connections or with close ties.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That relationship as a media representative came about as the result of an initiative that was undertaken by Dr. Koljevic back in 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: In September of 1993, Dr. Koljevic and I discussed the possibility of a more formal framework for such a relationship, but in fact it never materialised for a variety of logistic, financial and organisational reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That initiative was formalised in a proposal to Dr. Karadzic; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that "formalised" would be a precise term for something that was still in a preliminary and tentative form. It certainly never reached the form of -- of a detailed proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. In your testimony in the Popovic case, which I'm sure you recall since you published it on your web page, you said, and this is at page 25212 for the transcript, line 6, beginning at line 6, rather: "I therefore indicated to Professor Koljevic before he formalised the proposal to Dr. Karadzic that I would accept an informal arrangement in which my ability to continue with my other professional pursuits would not be hindered, and which would also enable me to present and articulate positions and analysis in accordance with my own understanding rather than in accordance with anyone's formal instructions." Do you remember saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you used word "formalised"; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: But it doesn't mean that the proposal had ever been formalised as such. What I said, that before Koljevic does so, he should bear in mind and then if you look at the rest of the sentence, it is quite obvious that I did not want to be a formal spokesman, that I, in fact, wanted to be free to articulate my views and positions without any interference from anyone else, which is in fact quite different from being either a spokesman or a representative.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We've got that, Dr. Trifkovic. But in fact, what you did is you arranged this particular scenario so that you could give the RS government and leadership plausible deniability.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, in order to reach this conclusion, we would need to go from what had been discussed between Professor Koljevic and me to what actually came to pass and --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, let me put it to you this way, then. What you said in your testimony in the Popovic case is, and I quote this, at page 25213, beginning at line 2: "I wanted to give them the ability to obtain plausible deniability." Do you dispute that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So that's -- that's one of the reasons why you reached this, quote/unquote, "informal arrangement" with Dr. Koljevic in relation to your media representations concerning the RS leadership --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Let me be very specific about the use of the term "plausible deniability." Because I didn't want to have any line of hierarchical command for my writings and media appearances, because I did not want to be subjected to anyone's articulation of positions which I would be obliged to follow, I didn't need plausible deniability, but in order to dispel any impression that my statements with which they may disagree are their own, the term "plausible deniability" referred specifically to their ability to say in good faith that Dr. Trifkovic does not represent Republika Srpska. And that, again, is tied in to what you said earlier about my being represented by some media as a spokesman, that, in fact, it was very important to avoid any such connection in order to preserve both my independence and their ability to dissociate themselves from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation. Your representation of the RS leadership's positions in the media was something that they never disagreed with you about; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, I don't even know if and to what extent they've been aware of all the media appearances I've had, and I've had quite a few, but at the same time, during my visits to Pale, my primary focus was to find out what's going on, to get Dr. Karadzic's and his advisors' assessment of the political, diplomatic, and military situation, and my media appearances were hardly ever even discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's very interesting, because in your Popovic testimony - and again I refer you and the Chamber to page 25213 - you specifically said you wanted to give them plausible deniability, as I've just said, in order to preserve their ability to distance themselves from your analysis as presented to the media, this is at line 6 and line 7, which by the way did not happen. That's true; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of them ever dissociating themselves from me, but I don't see what is so interesting, because I already dwelt on the subject of plausible deniability. I specifically wanted them to be able to dissociate themselves if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But they didn't?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Ever?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Ever meaning September '03 to July '05, yes, 22 months.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To this day, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I -- sorry, I don't understand the substance --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's all right.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that perhaps President Dodik should retroactively disassociate himself from my statements 17 years ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To this day you have not heard that the Republika Srpska leadership at any point ever dissociated themselves from your representations concerning them during the time that you were speaking to the media in their behalf --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: -- aware of any statements made to the media on their behalf ever, so the question is -- needs to be rephrased. I have never represented them, and I have never made statements to the media either purporting to represent them or doing so in substance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The French translation has only now been completed. Please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You maintained contacts with the RS leadership between 1993 and 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You also made media appearances in which you spoke about the positions of the RS leadership, specifically the events in the Balkans during the war from the Serbian point of view during that period of time; correct? You can answer that yes or no, sir.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It's -- it's a multilayered question, so I think that a yes or no is not in order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me break it down, then.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You made media appearances between 1993 and 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During those media appearances between 1993 and 1995, you gave analyses concerning the war?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You gave those analyses from the position of the Serbian point of view?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me refer you to your testimony in the Popovic case at transcript 252, line 25 and following. 25210, I'm sorry, lines 25 and following. You begin at the bottom of that page: "I was regularly interviewed, especially when it came to presenting a Serbian point of view in the ongoing conflicts in the former Yugoslavia." True?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During that period of time, you maintained this informal relationship with the Bosnian Serb leadership as you have described.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Before we go on, I really need to come back to your question and then the quote from the Popovic trial. It is one thing to give analysis from the position of the Serbian point of view. It is another to present a Serbian point of view in the context of interviews. In other words, my interviews were meant to provide an overall assessment within which I would present the Serbian point of view not necessarily as my own. Your question would imply that my media appearances were reflecting the Serbian point of view, whereas I insist that my media appearances were value neutral in the analytical sense but they were valuable to the media in that within those appearances I could authoritatively speak about what was the position, for instance, of the Bosnian Serb leadership. There is a distinction between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I appreciate that, sir. I'm just reading back what your testimony was four --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: And I am on the basis of that testimony explaining why the answer to your question "you gave those analyses from the Serbian point of view" was no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: During the period of time that you had --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I for transcript. The last answer was allocated to Excellency Kwon and it's not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It will be corrected later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You gave an interview in November 1994 to the BBC World Service's News Hour. During that period or during that interview you said this: "Nobody is taking into account the fact that Dr. Karadzic's overall strategy had always been that the Serbs do not want to occupy Muslim inhabited areas, that they simply want to separate themselves from the Muslims and to have three republics in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, possibly in the form of some loose union." Do you remember saying that, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember that specific programme, but this would be broadly something that I would say when asked about Dr. Karadzic's position.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In fact, you said basically that in your statement at paragraph 20, where you say one of Dr. Karadzic's views was that the Serb side did not want to defeat the Muslims militarily --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- but that each constituent nation should become master of its own fate; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is perfectly consistent with my previous answer. In other words, I don't remember that specific statement in that particular programme, but that would broadly reflect the position of Dr. Karadzic as I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And as you represented it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I never represented that position. As part of my analysis, I could also have said that President Izetbegovic's overall strategy is that there should be a centralised Bosnian state or that Milosevic's overall strategy -- so in other words, let us please not use the term "representation," because it would be misrepresenting my role and my journalistic activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: When I say "represent," I mean something that you said.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, in that sense, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. And you said it to the media.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On a number of occasions?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I think now's a good time for the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Now you realise how much of a pause you should put between the question and the answers. We will have a break for 45 minutes and resume at 17 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Trifkovic, when we left off I was asking you about some of the things you said to the media in this particular instance regarding the position or posture of the Bosnian Serb leadership while you were making various -- or giving various interviews and talks and so on. I want to show you 65 ter -- rather, P2085. Let me start by asking you -- I don't think we have the English on there yet. This, you can see, is a decision for further operations dated 24 November 1992. It is type-signed Colonel Milenko Milanovic, at that time the commander of the Drina Corps. Have you seen this document before, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Not to my recollection, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me just acquaint you with it a little bit. You can see that it's issued pursuant to the directive of the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska with a -- an order of the -- a directive, rather, of the confidential number 02/5 of 19 November 1992. And it says, at paragraph 1: To launch an attack using the main body of troops and major equipment to inflict on the enemy the highest possible losses, exhaust them, break them up, or force them to surrender, and force the Muslim local population to abandon the area of Cerska, Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde. Are you familiar with this operation, if not this order?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not specifically. I have no idea what this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: To force the local Muslim population to abandon the areas of Cerska, Zepa, Srebrenica, and Gorazde is not consistent with the things you were saying in the media in 1994, is it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It would not have been consistent had I been aware of some other policy in place. It was consistent with not only what I was told and conveyed but what other academic analysts and journalists were made to believe or understand on the basis of meetings with Dr. Karadzic. In addition, you're talking about a document from the fall of 1992, and the quote from that News Night interview referred to sometime two years later. Had I been privy to confidential and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask that you step back from the microphone, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Trifkovic, did you hear that? Could you distance yourself from the microphone. You are too close to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Had I been privy to top-secret documents from the Republika Srpska military, then indeed it would have made my task so much more interesting because that would indicate a certain degree of contradiction between the military orders and the line taken by the political powers that be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You are aware, of course, that Dr. Karadzic said that he signed off on Directives 1 through 7 at least?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please provide a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's the 54th Assembly session minutes. I can be more specific if the Chamber finds it necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you familiar with Dr. Karadzic having said that, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I would need to be reminded what specifically are those seven directives.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll let the Chamber worry about that. At P1415, e-court page 84 through 86 in English, and 108 through 111 in B/C/S, Dr. Karadzic said: "I have examined, approved, and signed seven directives. No one submitted the eighth and the ninth to me."

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Apparently this refers to a session of the Republika Srpska National Assembly from October of 1995, and my last meeting with Dr. Karadzic prior to yesterday afternoon was on 14th of July, 1995. And with the beginning of NATO operations in August, my focus was already being transferred into -- back into academic sphere with the beginning of the 1995-1996 academic year. So I am not familiar with the minutes of the 54th session of the Republika Srpska National Assembly, because by that time I was no longer focusing on Bosnian events in -- to the same extent as previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So the answer is no. You're not --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: The answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- aware that he said that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me show you P838. The Chamber's heard a lot of evidence about this document. It's entitled "Directive for Further Operations Number 7," and it is signed by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: We will need to go to page 10 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S, I believe. And here in the English at the bottom you'll see there's a reference to the Drina Corps. Are we on page 8 in the B/C/S? Try 9 or 7, please. Bear with me one moment and I'll get you the B/C/S page. If it's all right with the Chamber, if we could just proceed with the English, I can get through this, I think, relatively quickly. I don't have the correct B/C/S reference in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Dr. Trifkovic, at the bottom of this paragraph you will see tasks that are directed to the Drina Corps, the same corps that Zivanovic commanded, that I showed you in the previous document, and in this particular document it provides for the -- it says: "By planned and well-thought-out combat activities, operations, create an unbearable situation of total insecurity with no hope of further survival or life for the inhabitants of Srebrenica and Zepa." Are you familiar with that language in this document?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I am familiar with that language which surfaced in subsequent years. I was not familiar with the document at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me take you to page 14 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was page 15 in B/C/S, Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And hopefully this will be page 21 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In this section you will see in the third paragraph from the bottom, it states that: "The relevant state and military organs responsible for work with UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations shall through the planned and unobtrusively restrictive issuing of permits, reduce and limit the logistic support of UNPROFOR to the enclaves and the supply of material resources to the Muslim population, making them dependent on our goodwill while at the same time avoiding condemnation by the international community and international public opinion." Have you seen that language before, and are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It's fair to say this is not consistent with what you were saying in 1994 concerning the policies of the Republika Srpska leadership?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It is not consistent with the position of the Republika Srpska leadership as conveyed to me by the leaders at the time. But let me repeat, I am not familiar with this document or with this language on paragraph third from bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Now, if I could just quickly go back. You indicated that you worked for "Chronicles" magazine. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you worked there for about 14 years?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Did you work for or did you have any association with the Lord Byron Foundation during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I've had all along, in fact, the position of executive director which is an unpaid voluntary position.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And the "Chronicles" magazine is a publication that's put out by the Rockford Institute?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You're aware that the Rockford Institute is a paleoconservative organisation that's been criticised by many people, including its former New York branch director, John Neuhaus?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he's referred to that movement, paleoconservative movement, as xenophobic, racist, and nativist?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It's up to Mr. Neuhaus to have his opinions. The fact that people say something about someone doesn't make it so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: But he said it; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thomas Fleming is the current president and editor of "Chronicles" magazine; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And he has been publicly denounced as an anti-Semite and Holocaust revisionist. Yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Such attacks I'm not specifically familiar with. Holocaust revisionist, no. I've heard of him being attacked for anti-Semitism but not for Holocaust revisionism, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask if you're familiar with this, then. A document or an article that he wrote dated 3rd August 2006, he stated: "Theories of history are matters of fact and reason. The fact that so many troublemakers of the past 150 years have been of Jewish extraction - Marx, Freud, the Neoconservatives - is certainly no argument in their favour. Jewish 'intellectuals' continue to be in the forefront of the movements that aim to destroy our religion and culture." It's a document or an article entitled "Mel, poor Mel," referring to Mel Gibson, I'm sure, dated 3rd August 2006. Are you familiar with that language?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I haven't read that article.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me put up 65 ter 24549, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm just going to refer you very quickly to the bottom -- or, rather, the last paragraph on the page where you can see the quote that I read out. Can you see it, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, except for the last bit of the last sentence. Q.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And maybe we can go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you see what I read out?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We'll move on. You continue to work with Mr. Fleming; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, you have your own set of writings, and you've been rather outspoken concerning your views of Islam and of Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Of Islam more than of Muslims, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you've written hundreds of articles, papers and similar materials on the subject?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You've made numerous appearances, interviews, conferences, lectures, and so on, concerning those views and subject matter?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And you've given talks to youth groups, college students in relation to those views; yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Youth groups? College students, yes, but I don't remember youth groups. But if you remind me, I'll happily confirm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to show you --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that it matters --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that it matters. But, okay, let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And your views are widely considered extreme? Yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Hateful?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And they're considered bigoted?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Anti-Islam?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Look --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You can answer yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No -- well, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a video of -- and it's very short. It's at 65 ter 40604. This of a talk that you gave to a group called Youth for Western Civilisation, from 21 October 2010, I believe -- or 2011.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: "Those among us who put their families and their neighbourhoods and their lands before all others are normal people. Those who tell them that their attachments should be global and their lands and neighbourhoods belong to the whole world are sick and evil. "They are the enemy and Jihad's objective allies, and it is up to the millions of normal people to stop the madness. The traitor class wants them to share its death-wish, to self-annihilate its people with a historical memory of a cultural identity and to make room for the post-human, monistic utopia spearheaded by the Jihadist fifth column. This crime, epitomised by Ground Zero mosque, can and must be stopped. "The founders of the United States overthrew the colonial government for offences that were far lighter than those of which the traitor class is guilty. "The alternative is decline, collapse and death, moral and spiritual first. "You'll know if the Ground Zero mosque is built that we are obviously dead."

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you recall that talk, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Chamber could hear very well what was said and I would inquire, Mr. President, because the volume was very low in my headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was just told that unfortunately there was no translation in French. This time because I note that transcript has been uploaded into e-court --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President, and I understood that the booths have copies of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we continue, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. Trifkovic, you refer to a traitor class, traitor class. In the context of your talk, I understand that to be people who generally are willing to extend respect and consideration to people of the Islamic --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, quite the contrary. I said specifically people who deny the validity and legitimacy of traditional forms of loyalty based upon the family, the community, and the nation. I referred to the traitor class specifically in reference to certain upholders of cultural ideological traits commonly known as -- under the label "multiculturalism" which sometimes goes to the extreme of denying the validity and legitimacy of traditional bonds of culture, language, identity, and the insistence that those loyalties need to become loyal -- sorry, global and universal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The multiculturalists.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: There are various levels of multiculturalism, but certainly I was referring to the form that specifically seeks or upholds the belief in a form of transnational global identity as the preferred final model.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this particular exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6098, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You wrote an article called "Banned from Canadistan"?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: 24 February 2011?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And just so the record is clear, you're referring to having been denied entry into the country of Canada?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In that article you wrote that: "It appears that my contacts with the Bosnian Serb leaders in the early 1990s -- or, rather, the early '90s makes me 'inadmissible' today. As it happens, I was never one of their officials, senior or otherwise." All right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And that's what you assert here today; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: By the way, that is what the board of immigration reviews agreed with, because on 18th of September, 2012, they adjudicated the case in my favour. And if you wish, I have the PDF of that decision on my laptop in the waiting-room.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: My question is: That's what you assert here today, Dr. Trifkovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please stand back from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. You're not hearing the interpreter's intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't hear anything at all. I couldn't even hear when the Registrar announced the P number of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the volume. Could you turn up the volume of the headphone? Do you hear me, Mr. Vanderpuye, now?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I hear you, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Trifkovic, you're being asked again to put some distance from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vanderpuye. Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The question was: Mr. Trifkovic, that's what you assert here today?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: By the way, do you walk around with that PDF with you at all times?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I walk around with my laptop a lot, and it just happens to be on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Had I intended to produce it, I would have said up-front. But since you raised the issue, I just mentioned it in passing and as an act of courtesy.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said that the reasons why you were denied basically boiled down to some spurious reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And if we want, we'll put that up. 65 ter 24546, and we'll have to go to paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Absolutely, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And you say in the article: "Why should the Canadian authorities suddenly decide to keep me out of the country now and for transparently spurious reasons," and you answer your own question, saying, "because the Muslims told them so." Your words?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: On that's the reason for the title "Canadistan"; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You mention that the immigration board adjudicated your case recently, yes?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: There were three hearings on April 2nd and 3rd --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I don't need the dates.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, on September 18th, the case was decided in my favour.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were in contact with Dr. Karadzic in 1994, as you indicated in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In January 1994, June 1994, September 1994; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I would have to check those dates but --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You don't remember?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Roughly I believe that to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were in contact with Dr. Karadzic in January 1995, March 1995, and July 1995?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: For the Chamber's benefit, those references are at P4368, English pages 3, 4, 46, 71, 72 respectively. And March 23rd, 1995, can be found at page 37 of P2242, and July at page 90 and 91 of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it his agenda recorded by --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President. For 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You were familiar enough with President Karadzic that you could actually pick up the telephone line in his office in July, as you indicate in your statement, without knowing who was on the other end?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I assumed that General Mladic would be on the other end and I asked Dr. Karadzic to speak to General Mladic and to ask him for a statement about Srebrenica after he has finished talking to him. So my request to pick up the auxiliary line was based on the assumption that it would be General Mladic on the other end and that I would be able to obtain a statement from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. You did pick up the phone line; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, I asked you before about the types of characterizations of your work you were aware of in the public domain. Have you been characterized in the public domain as a genocide denier?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Have you been characterized in the public domain as a plagiarist?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not that I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember testifying in the Stakic trial, Dr. Trifkovic? You can answer that yes or no.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And do you remember being confronted about your report during the course of that trial on cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And during the course of that cross-examination, were you not challenged as a plagiarist for having copied the works of other authors?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: It concerned a quote and not my own language.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You weren't challenged as a plagiarist for having plagiarised someone else's work in the Stakic trial? Is that your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But I deny the directness of the assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: All right. In 2008 you wrote an article, this one was called "Can the West Be Saved?" 10 May 2008. You said in that article: "Today's Europe does not create social and civilisation commonalities except on the basis of wholesale denial of old morays, disdain for inherited values, and an over-rejection of traditional culture. It creates the dreary sameness of antidiscrimination and tolerance." Your words?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Except that "Europe" should be in either italics or quotes because it refers to the European Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Your words?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You believe that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Of course, taken out of context, this does not convey the fullness of what I was talking about, and frankly, I see no relevance to my sworn testimony. I could also believe that Elvis is well and runs a pizza joint in Oahu, or that Neil Armstrong's landing on moon was faked. I don't see how my believes, however eccentric from your point of view they may seem, are relevant to my sworn testimony here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll let the Chamber worry about that.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we've been going on this way for a fairly long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you this. In that same article you say, and this is talking about respect for the Islamic faith or people of that persuasion: "If such respect continues to be extended by the elite class, by the end of the century there will be no 'Europeans' as members of ethnic groups that share the same language, culture, history, and ancestors, and inhabit lands associated with their names." You go on to say: "The shrinking native populations will be indoctrinated into believing or else simply forced into accepting of the democratic shift in favour of unassimilable and hostile aliens is actually a blessing that enriches their culturally deprived and morally unsustainable societies." Your words, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: My words, indeed, and not at all remarkable in the context of recent writings on the subject, including Mark Steyn and -- do you want me to quote some other authors who have been in the public domain saying similar things?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think my question was clear: Your words, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You believe it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this article. It's at 65 ter 4568.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll put it up, Mr. President. Thank you. You're referring to the quote, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll give it to you in just a second. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Any objection, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6099, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we have a break here, I have a request that the Chamber reconsider the amount of time that has been allocated to the Prosecution for the cross-examination of this witness and reduce it because I have to say, with all due respect to counsel, this has been one of the most empty cross-examinations that we've had. We've been going on for over an hour now and not even touched this topic of the meeting of the 13th and 14th of July, fishing around about contacts with the Defence for about 15 minutes, articles on his personal opinions. So I think obviously you gave them way too much time for this length of the statement and the scope of it. So I would ask that you give them ten more minutes and let's move on to something more productive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, does it not go to his credibility?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I think it does, but it's his beliefs and his positions that he's taken are only worth so much time of the Chamber. If you look at the times you told Dr. Karadzic to move on and compare it with what we've been listening to for the last hour, I think you'd have told him that ten times by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't remember the Chamber ever restricted his cross-examination on relevant issues. I'll consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber made a ruling to allow the Prosecution to use one and a half hours, and the Chamber is not minded at this time to limit his cross-examination in any event. Please continue, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Sir, you wrote an article in January 2007. It's called "Dinesh the Dhimmi."

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Do you remember that one?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in that article you quoted someone by the name of Bat Ye'or; right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You said that: "Only Islam has the ability to evoke this eagerly cringing attitude. Only Islam has this facility of inducing people to surrender psychologically to it even before it has any actual power over them." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: This sounds like Bat Ye'or's quote, not mine. Right?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpretation intervention: Could the document be placed on the screen before quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't hear what was said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking to upload the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes, 4578, please. Page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: First I would like to see the front page to see the title because it's not in the transcript. [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: At page 3 is the part that I read. Last paragraph, and it begins at just about the third line up from the bottom of that paragraph. It says: "Of all of the social, ethnic, religious, political movements ..." Do you see that, Dr. Trifkovic?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd like to tender this documents is well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6100, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: In another article, 65 ter 4572, you call Islam a psychosis. Do you recall using those words, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Before we proceed, what you quoted in the previous article was a quote and not my own language, but I obviously used it approvingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You subscribe to it. You believe it?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Broadly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You referred to Islam as a psychosis. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: This was an article that you wrote in November 2003. It is 65 ter 4572. And that you believe as well; correct?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: The term "Islam is psychosis" was first used in fact by Dr. Quill [phoen] in his writings about his trips in North Africa in the 1840s, as far as I can remember. But, yes, I did say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: And if given a chance, I would like to elaborate what exactly I mean by that term.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me ask you about a different article. This one's called "Islamic Terrorism in Italy, The Shape of Things to Come." It's from 27 February 2002. In this article - it's 65 ter 4573 - you say: "The old liberal secular antipathy to Christianity has converged with the new PC movement and the therapeutic society to produce a climate wherein it is easy for the Muslims to lie about the nature of Islam." Your words?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Oh, dear. Everything out of context. Yes, my words, absolutely, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Page 3, for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These words out of context have not entered the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You go on to say, just under the part where it says, "Britain leads the way": "Islam has never learned to live as a minority. It simply cannot reconstruct itself in Western societies." And on page 5, you say: "If and when the Constitutional Court," referring to Germany, "allows clitoridectomy for Muslim girls, presumably another important step will be made, but that integration will complete only when Pakistanis in Britain, Algerians in France, and Turks in Germany turn the host country into an Islamic society by compelling it to adapt to their way of life." Right?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll tender this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: You have a solution to keep that from happening, Dr. Trifkovic, isn't that right? And that's --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: I wish there was one, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, the one you've proposed is to deport citizens, immigrants alike of Islamic background --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- out of --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Those engaged in Islamist activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I finish my question, sir?

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you. Your solution is to deport citizen and immigrant alike that are Muslims --

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: -- out of Western countries.

utterances.speaker: SRDJAN TRIFKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Let me play you 65 ter 24539.
